findings.title: Public `findMany` removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions`, so existing callers lose their API
findings.body:
The PR deletes `findMany(findManyArgs)`, which ran `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the auth and filter conditions merged into `where`. Its replacement, `getBaseConditions()`, returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any caller still using `service.findMany(...)` (e.g. insights tRPC handlers) will fail to compile or break at runtime.

The returned fragment also cannot be merged into a Prisma `where` object. Every consumer must be rewritten to `$queryRaw` and re-implement select, ordering and pagination by hand. These call sites should be migrated in the same PR, or `findMany` kept until they are.

findings.title: Constructor now accepts a loose options type, losing compile-time checks
findings.body:
The constructor parameter changed from the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional regardless of `scope`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team" }` without `teamId` and it type-checks. The Zod parse then fails and the service silently returns `1=0`, i.e. zero results with no error.

Previously the compiler rejected this. The silent empty result makes misconfiguration hard to diagnose.

findings.title: Org-scope test depends on unordered DB result ordering
findings.body:
The expected SQL embeds arrays in a fixed order: `[org, team, team2, team3]` and `[user, user2, user3]`. The service builds these arrays from `teamRepo.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, with deduplication via a Set. Neither query appears to use an ORDER BY, so Postgres may return rows in a different order.

Because `toEqual` compares the Sql `values` positionally, the test can fail intermittently even when the service is correct. Sort the arrays in the service, or compare them order-independently.

findings.title: Caching tests removed though caching behaviour is unchanged
findings.body: The `Caching` describe block was deleted entirely. The service still memoizes `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`. Those tests could have been adapted to the Sql format. Removing them drops coverage of the memoization, including the `null` filter case that relies on the `=== undefined` check.
